item.title: What to do about illegal subletters
item.description: Some rules are meant to be broken. Consider this message I received from an owner of rent-stabilized buildings: “There are countless units that have been in the same tenant’s name or family for decades while their needs and family makeup have changed. For example, they have a 3 or 4 bedroom apartment for a family of 1 and perhaps 2. item.title: Mark Nussbaum turns on former “bro” Tzali Chopp over unpaid debt
item.description: Disgraced attorney and fixer Mark Nussbaum is turning against his former friend and deal partner as creditors seek to collect more than $400 million in missing escrow funds. Sheldon Eisenberger, an attorney handling the wind-down and liquidation of Nussbaum’s former law firms, has launched a lawsuit against nursing home entrepreneur and Nussbaum’s former friend Tzali Chopp of Opal Healthcare. item.title: Brooklyn townhouse development darling expands to Manhattan
item.description: One of Brownstone Brooklyn’s most active townhouse developers is trying to make it in Manhattan. Eckstrom, the eight-year-old development firm run by husband and wife duo Carlos Saavedra and Nicole Eckstrom, is expanding into the city with two West Village properties. item.title: City environmental agency relocates next to polluted waterway
item.description: New York City’s Department of Environmental Protection found a fitting home in Long Island City. Through the Department of Citywide Administrative Services, DEP signed a lease for 155,000 square feet at Innovo Property Group’s 24-02 49th Avenue, the Commercial Observer reported. The agency will use the space for offices and laboratories. The building is along the Newtown Creek, which flows into the East River. item.title: Olayan Group nabs $800M loan for 550 Madison
item.description: The Olayan Group locked in an $800 million loan for its revamped Midtown office building, better known as the Sony building. ING Capital added $230 million of new debt to the existing $570 million loan balance on 550 Madison Avenue, according to property records. ING issued the original loan in 2016, when Olayan purchased the 41-story, 800,000-square-foot Midtown building between East 55th and East 56th streets for $1.4 billion. item.title: Roosevelt Hotel gets a surprising new partner: the US government
item.description: Just when it appeared Pakistan was back at square one in figuring out the future of the Roosevelt Hotel, an unexpected partner came along: the White House. item.title: Bronx housing project tests out ballot measure’s speedier approval process
item.description: A housing project in the Bronx will go through a speedier land use review process, the first to test out one of three housing-related ballot measures approved by voters in November. The Powerhouse Apartments project will go through the Expedited Land Use Review Procedure, or Elurp, which will last 90 days instead of the usual 200-plus days required under the Uniform Land Use Review Procedure.
